notes.compared_quantity: Phase 1 (setup) + phase 2 (evaluation), for the FEM's scalar solve and for the finite-Peclet series, producing the scalar at every mesh node.
notes.momentum_excluded: The Navier-Stokes solve is measured and reported under not_compared. It never enters a compared total, a ratio or a figure: the velocity field is prescribed analytically and the series never computes one.
notes.phase0_excluded: Interpreter start-up, library imports, mesh reading and the driver's Python boundary-condition loops are reported and never compared.
notes.speedups_are_lower_bounds: The CPU governor cannot be pinned without root, so a 1-thread run boosts to a higher clock than an 8-thread one. Raw speedups therefore understate the true ones; the calibration-kernel ratio gives the normalised value.
notes.fem_error: Each FEM solution is scored once against a reference: the finite-Peclet series at beta_max = 400 with no mode cutoff, at the nodes of the same mesh. E = ||psi_ref - psi_h|| / ||psi_ref||, discrete 2-norms over the interior nodes (not on the inlet, the outlet or the wall). Computed after every timed run, in its own process, never timed. The benchmarked series (beta_max = 200) is never differenced against the FEM.
notes.series_measured_at_every_peclet: The series is measured at every Peclet number, never extrapolated from one. Its mode count is the same at all of them (2550 at beta_max = 200), but Pe changes the modified roots and therefore the eigenfunctions: measured setup varies 1.9x and evaluation 1.4x across Pe = 10/100/1000, non-monotonically, with Pe = 100 the cheapest.
notes.finite_peclet_only: Only setup_fp_solution() is called. setup_bare_solution() and setup_qep_solution() are never invoked, and the worker asserts SolutionMethod.ModifiedRoots before evaluating.

memory_cross_check_vs_usr_bin_time.note: Not a two-sided agreement test: clear_refs clobbers the kernel high-water mark that /usr/bin/time -v reads, so the external figure under-reports by construction. Use process_peak_rss_bytes.

fem_error_once_per_case.note: Every FEM solution is scored exactly once against the reference (ERROR_REFERENCE), after every timed run. The benchmarked series fields are never differenced against the FEM.
